Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Our music department has been busier than ever this Christmas with Christmas concerts, carols in care homes and X-Factor.
Over the past few weeks we have enjoyed performances from our jazz band, orchestras, guitar group, flute quartet, brass group, string group, djembe drummers, girls choirs, boys choirs, chamber choir, rock bands and more!
Very well done to all of the children who have filled the school with glorious sounds over the festive period and thank you to the marvellous Miss Baker and her talented team of music teachers who support and inspire our pupils each and every day.

Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Our Summer Serenade, ‘A Night at the Movies’, showcased the wonderful musical talents of our Port Regians.From choirs and orchestras to brass, strings, flute, guitar and jazz, pupils across the school came together for an evening of music in FMS in the final week of the school year.The varied programme of pieces on the popular movies theme illustrated the breadth of music opportunities, not least through the sheer variety of groups and choirs - Brass Group, Training Orchestra, Senior Boys' and Girls' Choirs, Flute Group, Guitar Group, Jazz Band, Chamber Choir, String Group and School Orchestra. Toe tapping pieces included the Theme From Apollo 13, Over the Rainbow, Memory and The Great Escape. A fitting close was the Combined Orchestra and Choirs joining for a memorable performance of A Million Dreams.What a super evening, well done to all our young musicians, and thank you to our brilliant Music Department for such a special event celebrating music making for all ages at Port Regis.

pageCache.pageTitle: Board of Governors | Port Regis School
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Port Regis is governed by a Board of Governors, called our 'Council of Management', whose prime responsibility is to ensure that the School provides the best education for the children. The Council has a duty to ensure its charitable objectives are adhered to. It comprises a group of people who voluntarily contribute a varied and differing range of experiences and skills applicable to the functions of the School. The Council seeks to achieve a balanced and diverse membership.
The full Council meets once a term although much of its work is carried out through committees which meet on a regular basis and report to the Council.
The Chair can be contacted via the Clerk to Governors by email at clerk@portregis.com or by post to: The Bursary, Port Regis, Motcombe Park, Shaftesbury, Dorset, SP7 9QA.
James joined the Council of Management as Chair of Governors in Summer 2021.
James read Modern History at Oxford before joining De La Rue Plc , a global industrial, as a graduate trainee in 1983; he remained with De La Rue for a further 27 years becoming CEO in 2009, a business with £500m of revenue and in the FTSE250.
In 2011, James joined Oberthur Fiduciaire a family business in the same industry as De La Rue, based in Paris, as Advisor to the Chairman, a post which he held for 9 years until December 2020. James has also been a Non-Executive Director of Camelot, the UK National Lottery; Vice Chairman of a charity, Friends of the Elderly and remains a Trustee for Ruffer LLP (Capital Points)
James is married to Emma, lives in Wiltshire and is an former Port Regis parent.
Committee: As Chair, James is a member of all Committees. He can be contacted via email at james.hussey@portregis.com.
Emily has worked at Wycombe Abbey School since 2008. She is currently Deputy Head (Academic), responsible for all aspects of the School's academic life; she was previously Director of Higher Education and Careers. Before that, she was Head of Religious Studies at Cheltenham Ladies' College. She enjoys teaching across the whole range from 11-18 and is keen to encourage pupils to read widely and to find their own passion. Emily was educated at boarding school from the age of 10 and later read Theology at Worcester College, Oxford. She met her husband David at Oxford and they have a 6 year old daughter, Emily's interests include music and travel. She is a member of our Education Committee.
Committee: Emily is Chair of the Education Committee.
Giles is experienced in solving problems and leading change in both large and small firms, with a focus around technology and finance. He has worked with the leading global firms in the financial services industry.
Driven by a desire to identify and utilise the most productive technology for business, or, in our case Port Regis, Giles will help us create teams who can work efficiently and autonomously with the right tools to find sustainable solutions for complex school and education issues. Giles will bring a technology and IT understanding to the workings of the school and the Council of Management.
Giles has one child at Port Regis.
Committee: Giles is Chair of the Marketing & Admissions Committee.
Rupert was educated at Sherborne School and Reading University where he read History. He retired from the Army in 2022 as a Major General after 30 years' service. He commanded on operations in Northern Ireland, Bosnia, Iraq. Afghanistan, Syria and the Caribbean. Decorated twice on operations, among other senior roles served as the Army's Assistant Chief of the General Staff and as deputy commander of the US-led coalition that defeated ISIS.
He now lives in Somerset and works as a consultant and advisor. His three children all attended Port Regis.
Committee: Rupert is Chair of the Governance Committee and is a member of the Finance Committee.
Will was educated at St Paul's School before studying at the University of St Andrew's and later competing an MEd in Educational Leadership at the University of Buckingham. He has taught in a wide range of settings, including five years in Sydney, Australia, and earlier in the state sector in London, where he also served as a teacher governor.
At Milton Abbey School, Will has held senior roles including Deputy Head Cocurricular, Housemaster and Head of Lower School. He has also served as Chair of Governors at Cheselbourne Village School and as a member of the Advisory Board at Yarrells Prep.
Will lives in Dorset with his family
Committee: Will is the Chair of the Wellbeing & Safeguarding Committee, and is also the Safeguarding Governor.
Christa is a leading litigation lawyer with more than 30 years in practice, during which time she has taught law, practised as a barrister, and worked for leading international firms both in the UK and overseas. She has a first class degree in law from Cambridge University and a first class post-graduate Bachelor of Civil Law degree from Oxford University.
Christa was on the Partnership Board of Linklaters for six years from 2009 and was appointed to the Council of Management at Port Regis in 2024. Her two daughters were educated at Port Regis.
Committee: Christa is a member of the Education Committee
William was educated at Harrow School and the University of East Anglia, where he read law. He was a practicing solicitor for some 25 years, working as a shipping litigator with Richards Butler and then with, and as a partner of, Reed Smith LLP.
William now lives in Tollard Royal in Wiltshire. He is married to Rebecca, a commercial barrister. He and Rebecca have two teenage children, the younger of which attended Port Regis.
Committee: William is a member of the Governance Committee.
Alastair was brought up in Wiltshire and attended Marlborough College and University College London where he read Mechanical Engineering. After a year working in the City for Hambros Bank, Alastair joined the Army and spent five years in the Royal Horse Artillery where he served in Canada, the Czech Republic, France, Jamaica, Oman and the UK. After leaving the Army, Alastair completed an MBA at London Business School and has spent the last 24 years in commercial roles at a variety of large companies (Economist Group, Bloomberg, Reed Elsevier) and smaller, private equity-backed businesses. Alastair is married with two children and lives in the Chalke Valley.Committee: Alastair is a member of the Finance Committee.
Rupert was educated at The Oratory School and Durham University where he read Law & Politics. After qualifying as a solicitor, Rupert worked in the City for 11 years, first as a associate in a City law firm, and then in the private banking arm of a leading bank.
After becoming a partner in a Top 10 ranked UK National law firm, Rupert moved to the Channel Islands, where he was Head of Legal at a leading private bank, and then European Head of Wealth Management Compliance at Royal Bank of Canada.
Now semi-retired, Rupert works part time for Jersey Finance Limited, the promotional arm of the Jersey Government. An avid military historian, Rupert regularly speaks at clubs and societies on military history topics, with a particular interest in post Second World War British counterinsurgency campaigns. Rupert's first book 'The Soldiers' General', the biography of Lieutenant General Sir George Lea, was published in March 2025.
Committee: Rupert is a member of the Governance Committee.
Henrietta read Classics at Trinity College, Cambridge. She worked in Investment Management for 18 years, first at Flemings and later at UBS and Putnam Investments. In 2010 she moved into education, teaching Classics at the Thomas's schools in London, and was Head of Classics at Thomas's Clapham.
Henrietta has been a trustee of Kensington Aldridge Academy in London since 2022.
Henrietta moved to Dorset in 2023 and lives close to Port Regis with her husband Archie and four children.
Committee: Henrietta is a member of the Finance Committee.
Helen is a passionate and enthusiastic educationalist; she has spent four decades working in education both in the maintained and independent sectors. Helen has experience of teaching and senior leadership positions in prep and senior schools in the UK and overseas. Helen has experience of day and boarding schools, co-educational and single sex schools and is particularly interested in the educations of the very youngest pupils, those in pre-prep.
Helen retired from headship in June 2022, having been Head of Sunny Hill Prep School (Somerset) for fourteen years. Prior to this she had worked for eight years at The Berlin British School and before this in two large comprehensive schools.
Helen has been an ISI Team Inspector in the UK and overseas for over ten years. She is also a Regional Support Representative for IAPS (Independent Association of Prep Schools).
Helen and her family live in Somerset.
Committee: Helen is a member of the Wellbeing Committee and Education Committee and is also the EYFS Governor.
Guy is Head of Financial Markets at ING Bank London, with extensive experience leading global trading and structuring teams across all Financial products in both emerging and developed markets.
He holds a Biochemistry degree from London University, with additional studies in Mathematics and Computing.
He is married to Jane and they have three children, Wilf & Ned who are currently at Sherborne (previously at Port Regis) and Mia who is at Port Regis. The family are primarily based in Somerset but Guy works in London during the week.
Committee: Guy is a member of the Finance Committee.
Alex teaches Geography at Eton College where he has been since 2003 and is currently House Master of Jourdelay’s which he took on in 2017. He has degrees from Oxford, Nottingham and Cambridge universities.
In another life, he was an international oarsman and coach, rowing and coaching for Great Britain and latterly coaching for Australia where he lived for three years in Melbourne. He has run the high performance section of Eton’s rowing program for twelve years. He is also a governor at Ludgrove School.
Alex is married to Rachael, an educational fundraiser with whom he has a son, Bligh currently at St Edward’s School in Oxford. They have their family home in Hazelbury Bryan, Dorset.
Committee: Alex is a member of the Education Committee.
Motcombe ParkShaftesburyDorsetSP7 9QAUnited Kingdom

pageCache.pageTitle: Visits & Open Mornings | Port Regis Independent Prep School
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Open Mornings
Nothing quite beats being here and discovering the Port Regis experience for yourself.
We know that choosing a school is a big decision and we want families to have every opportunity to get a feel for Port Regis. We offer both individual family visits and group Open Mornings through the school year.
Our Open Mornings are small group events held a number of times a year and are a more informal opportunity for you to come and experience the school on a working day, hear from our Headmaster, meet staff and pupils and take a tour of our grounds and facilities. They are generally held on a Friday so that you can see the whole school in full swing on a normal day, including our Nursery and Pre-Prep.
Children are very welcome to come along too. Equally our Open Mornings are a chance to revisit the school following an individual visit. We limit numbers to ensure that each family can gain as much from the morning as possible, so we encourage you to book early if you would like to come to one of these.
Our next Open Morning for both Prep and Pre-Prep entry will be held on Friday 2nd October 2026. Please click the booking link below to complete the booking form.
If you are unable to make our Open Morning or would like to visit us before October please do get in touch with our Head of Admissions, Stephanie Fone, via admissions@portregis.com or 01747 857914 who would be delighted to arrange a private visit to the school.
If you are unable to attend an Open Morning we would be more than happy to arrange a private tour at a date and time convenient to you. Please contact our Head of Admissions, Stephanie Fone, on admissions@portregis.com or 01747 857914 to arrange a visit.

Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Book for our Open Morning on Friday 2nd October 2026
We would be delighted to welcome you to our Open Morning on Friday 2nd October. We deliberately hold our Open Mornings on a Friday so that families can see the whole school in full swing on a normal working day, including our Nursery and Pre-Prep.
Please complete the booking form below to book your place.
The outline format for our Open Morning is as follows:
09:00: Arrival and coffee
09:15: Welcome from the Headmaster
09:30-10:15: Individual guided tours of the school by two current pupils (Pre-Prep - tours by staff)
10:15-11:30: Teaching staff, senior leadership and boarding staff available to answer your questions over coffee after your tour
11:30: Open Morning ends
There will be displays in departments for children to see during the tour, so they are very welcome to come along.
Free Shuttle Bus from Gillingham Train Station
If you are travelling by train, Port Regis is just 10 minutes from Gillingham (Dorset) train station. It is on the mainline from Exeter to London Waterloo. A free shuttle bus service to and from the station is available - please indicate on your booking form if you are interested in this option.
If you would like to book overnight accommodation, we have special rates with a number of local hotels. Please ask us for more details.
If you have any questions please do contact us via admissions@portregis.com

It's a real privilege to lead our Pre-Prep and Nursery and I look forward to igniting your child’s imagination and hearing the sound of their laughter as they have fun while learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-Prep Sport & Physical Wellbeing | Port Regis
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Building Foundational Skills
All young children need to run around and have space to express themselves. Our sports programme allows them to do this while developing core strength, stability, physical co-ordination and social skills and team building.
Our Pre-Prep and Nursery children receive several sports lessons a week led by specialist sports staff. In the Nursery and Reception, these lessons include swimming, ball skills, gymnastics and dance. In the older years, we mirror our prep school sporting curriculum as closely as possible, so lessons also include netball, hockey, football, cricket and athletics. And after school there’s always a variety of clubs and hobbies to enjoy.
Throughout the year we have a range of Pre-Prep and Nursery sporting events including cross country, gym competitions and our very own triathlon and in true fashion, our summer term culminates in our high anticipated Pre-Prep Sports Day!
No day would be complete at Port Regis without the award-winning food freshly cooked on site by our experienced chefs. Every day, they prepare three delicious and nutritious meals and two snacks, catering for a broad range of dietary and religious requirements.
Menus include favourites like pad thai and paella as well as healthy home-made soups, vegetarian curries and a hand carved roast with all the trimmings. There’s always a huge salad bar and – as part of our sustainable food programme – our termly 30-mile lunch menu is made using ingredients from local suppliers.
Motcombe ParkShaftesburyDorsetSP7 9QAUnited Kingdom

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Sport & Physical Wellbeing | Port Regis School
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
From exploration to excellence
Our number one priority is to help every child enjoy sport. And the sheer variety of what’s on offer means they are sure to find something they’ll love – whether that’s rugby, cricket, hockey, fencing, golf and even quidditch!
From Reception to Year 8, Port Regis children have the opportunity to take part in sport every day. By making it fun and engaging, we sow the seed for a healthy, lifelong relationship with physical activity.
As they move through the school, children also learn the benefits of competition. We have a busy calendar of competitive fixtures for Years 3 to 8. As well as a great way of improving skills, these matches are an opportunity to socialise with other children, build empathy and sportsmanship.
At the heart of our approach to sport are the Four Es: Explore, Enjoy, Engage, Excel.
We believe that sport is for everyone. Watch our video to see sport in action as well as hear our values for sport.
From the moment children join the prep school, they are encouraged to explore the many activities on offer. With more than 30 sports available to try, these early years are a time of rapid physical, social and mental development.
Port Regis has always been known for the strength of its sports teams. However, we understand that traditional sports are not for everyone and our main aim is for all children to find a sport they enjoy. So we take a varied multi-sport approach to the curriculum, offering activities including triathlons, gymnastics, lacrosse, yoga, basketball, quidditch and dance.
Children who enjoy sport are naturally more engaged, more focused in games sessions and more prepared for taking on new challenges. Our coaches aim to capture that interest and inspire pupils to achieve their potential. Focusing on each child's development so that their individual achievements and successes can be recognised.
Through enjoyment and engagement, we hope that pupils will strive for excellence in sport with each pupil reaching their fullest potential, whether that be beating their personal best (PB) or competing nationally. with many going on to gain Sports Scholarships to senior schools. For these pupils we offer scholarship preparation including, fitness testing, sports psychology and nutrition.
Something for everyone
Our superb facilities include the pitches and courts you’d expect and more: a competition grade gymnasium, 25-metre heated indoor swimming pool, mountain bike and BMX track, assault course and skateboard ramp.
We’re delighted to host regular national and international competitions, including IAPS netball, rugby 7s, athletics, gymnastics and swimming galas. For more information about our facilities click here.
Encouraging a healthy, active lifestyle
To us, sport is about more than PBs and trophies. It’s about laying the foundations for children to become healthy, active teenagers and adults. This is why we also teach children about nutrition, show how to stretch and relax through activities like yoga and we we invest in the Corefulness programme from Reception.
To see an example timetable of sport and PE throughout the year click here.
No day would be complete at Port Regis without the award-winning food freshly cooked on site by our experienced chefs. Every day, they prepare three delicious and nutritious meals and two snacks, catering for a broad range of dietary and religious requirements.
Menus include favourites like pad thai and paella as well as healthy home-made soups, vegetarian curries and a hand carved roast with all the trimmings. There’s always a huge salad bar and – as part of our sustainable food programme – our termly 30-mile lunch menu is made using ingredients from local suppliers.

Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Holiday Clubs at Port Regis
We offer fun and creative days for children to enjoy during each school holiday, and often at half terms too. All sessions are held within Port Regis School and grounds and will make use of the fantastic facilities available.
Information about our half term and holiday clubs will be published nearer the dates but if you have any questions please contact office@portregis.com.
Swim and Gym Programme
We provide structured swimming lessons and gym classes to children of all ages. All swimming sessions are held in our 25m heated pool while gym classes make use of our competition grade gymnasium and Level 2 gym coaches. We have a spacious viewing balcony and easy on-site parking.
Please contact sportscentre@portregis.com for more information.
Motcombe ParkShaftesburyDorsetSP7 9QAUnited Kingdom

Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Nurturing their creativity
Children love to dance, paint, and construct imaginative models. We make sure they can do all these and much more. Our Pre-Prep and Nursery arts curriculum includes dance, music and art, as well as after-school clubs in everything from tap and ballet to chess and golf.
In the early years children sing and learn how to use simple instruments like tambourines and triangles. In Years 1 and 2 they can learn a musical instrument including piano. recorder, percussion, or violin.
Drama also plays a key role. As well as developing key speaking, listening and confidence skills, the Pre-Prep productions, led by Head of Drama, Lia Matthews, are a highlight for children and parents alike.
Getting closer to nature
Our purpose-built Forest School is the perfect start to encouraging a love of the outdoors - an opportunity for children to study all those amazing mini-beasts and hone their gardening skills. We also organise lots of interesting trips, Exploration of our school grounds is a key part of learning in the Pre-Prep. Each week, the whole of Pre-Prep and Nursery venture outside to our purpose built forest school for Forest Fridays. We take special notice of the abundant wildlife which populates our school grounds, from woodpeckers and barn owls, to badgers and deer - plus our own school animals including sheep, chicken, rabbits and guinea pigs!
Our beautiful Rose Garden is at the centre of the school and not only provides a beautiful space for free play but is also home to our garden and greenhouse for growing a range of fruit and vegetables which are used in our kitchens.
Hobbies
Hobbies are available after school for children in Years 1 and 2 including fencing, tennis and modern dance. In the summer term, a selection of hobbies are also available to our children in Reception, including ballet, yoga and art.
Children in Years 1 and 2 may also learn a musical instrument including piano, recorder, percussion or violin, with specialist teachers.
Motcombe ParkShaftesburyDorsetSP7 9QAUnited Kingdom

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular & Enrichment | Port Regis Prep School
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
A Port Regis Education plus so much more
PR Plus is an exciting element in our Saturday morning timetable.
At its heart, Port Regis champions dynamic learning that equips children to lead fulfilling and rewarding lives. For this learning to remain relevant, our curriculum must be both broad and ambitious. It must inspire not only the mind, but the head, the hand and the heart. It must stretch pupils within, and beyond, the classroom.
Historically, Saturday mornings have focused exclusively on academic lessons. The purpose of PR Plus is to create some more time to enable our children to develop new skills through a range of vocational, intellectual and collaborative activities.
As a preparatory school, Port Regis seeks to prepare children not only for exam success but, more importantly, to succeed in life in all its fullness. As our long-standing motto proclaims: ‘We seek higher things’. PR Plus enables us to do just that – with renewed purpose and opportunity.
Our PR Plus programme is an example of the tremendous range of learning on offer: from talks about Chaucer, famous works of art, Plato, entrepreneurship, anthropology, film making and managing one’s finances; to how to wash your clothes, make a bed and cook a crumble. There were workshops on first aid, fire safety, communication skills, Black History month and leadership, alongside creative and environmental projects, orienteering and community work in Motcombe village.
Our hobbies programme is renowned for the breadth that's on offer, every day. This enriches the lives of the children, teaches them new skills and gives the chance for them to develop their talents whatever direction that catches their interest.
Pupils can choose from over 70 activities, a mix of free and paid, children can experience anything from soap and jewellery making to beekeeping, campfire cooking and chicken whispering! Below is just a small selection of what's on offer from Year 1 upwards, tailored to the different age groups:
Lego and Construction
Cook your own supper
There are also extra games practice, maths and language clubs and additional ISEB pre-test support within the programmes which run through each week.

Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
The Grosvenor girls were excited to get their hands on the BSA Award for ‘Boarding Innovation of the Year’ last night! This was awarded in recognition of the introduction of ‘Self-Care Tuesdays’ – a simple yet important innovation which normalises pupils looking after their mental and physical wellbeing as they head into their teenage years. Thank you Boarding Schools' Association and bravo to our brilliant boarding team for working tirelessly to maintain and strengthen the excellent boarding provision at Port Regis.

pageCache.pageTitle: Port Regis commended for Boarding School of the Year 2026
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
We were thrilled to receive the news at the end of the summer term that Port Regis has been commended in the Boarding School of the Year category in this year's Independent Schools of the Year awards.
We were selected from among both senior and prep schools in this category. Judges were looking for schools that truly have boarding 'running through their DNA', a full commitment to boarding and why boarders enjoy an experience like no other.
To be selected for the final against independent schools from across the country would be a huge honour and testament to Port Regis' commitment to boarding school life. The announcement of finalists will be in early September - fingers crossed!

pageCache.pageTitle: Port Regis named Top 3 Boarding Preps in the UK
pageCache.text:
Come and see why Port Regis is a Top 3 UK Boarding Prep School
Described as ‘One of the Great Prep Schools’, we are thrilled to share that Port Regis has been named one of the Top 3 Boarding Prep Schools in the UK in the prestigious The Week ‘Best of the Best Independent Schools’ Guide 2026.
Founded in 1881, Port Regis gives children a rare blend of joyful, unhurried childhood and ambitious, specialist‑led teaching. Its curriculum is bold, creative and academically rigorous — and it shows. In the past three years, our Year 8 leavers have achieved 93 scholarships to leading senior schools across the country.
Boarding is at the heart of school life, with over 70% of pupils boarding in some form from Year 3. The result is a vibrant, seven‑day‑a‑week community packed with activities, friendships and opportunities. Local day pupils are equally welcome — and in Years 3 and 4 can even board for two nights a week free of charge through the school’s ‘local day boarder’ offer.
Set within 150 acres of stunning Dorset countryside, with daily bus routes across Dorset and Somerset, Port Regis is a true home from home where children can flourish.
Headmaster Titus Mills commented:
“What an absolute honour to have been recognised by The Week in the top 3 in the UK. Everyone who is part of our Port Regis community can feel rightly very proud. As a truly independent prep boarding school which also welcomes day pupils, what we offer children here is a very special childhood, encouraging every boy and girl from age 2 to 13 to learn values of Joy, Generosity, Courage, Creativity and Endeavour. We are able to give them the time and space to do this through the boarding school ethos, with a huge range of opportunities inside and outside the classroom.”
